prompt:
An eight-panel comic strip with clean ink borders, TWO ROWS OF FOUR panels. All eight panels are the same bakery kitchen seen from a different angle each time, with the same baker in a white coat and brown apron at work. On a shelf behind him stands a single white JUG and above the bench hangs a LAMP.

THE JUG DECAYS IN TWO ONE-WAY STEPS, and it never recovers:
  * in panels 1 and 2 the jug is WHOLE and undamaged.
  * in panel 3 it has been knocked and now has a big CRACK drawn across it, but it is still standing in one piece — and it is still the same cracked jug in panels 4 and 5.
  * in panel 6 it has fallen and lies on the shelf in BROKEN PIECES, and it is still in broken pieces in panels 7 and 8. It never goes back to being cracked-but-whole, and never back to undamaged.

THE LAMP: switched OFF (dull and grey) in panel 1; from panel 2 onwards it is GLOWING and it stays glowing to the end.

The two changes start in different panels. His pose and the framing change every panel. No text, no captions, no lettering.
easy_question: This image was supposed to show a comic strip: several separate panels, drawn side by side, with the same person appearing in each panel. Ignoring artistic quality and ignoring whether the story is right, does the image DEPICT that — a strip of separate panels with a recurring figure? A comic page, a storyboard or a picture-book strip all count as yes. Answer NO only if it is blank, a single picture with no panels, or something unrelated. Answer yes or no only.

reference.qa: This picture is a comic strip of 8 panels arranged as two rows of four panels. Look at every panel in reading order (the top row left to right, then the bottom row left to right). For EACH panel in that order, report what state the white jug on the shelf behind the baker is in — in one piece and undamaged, in one piece but with a crack drawn across it, or lying in broken pieces. Use only these words: whole, cracked, broken. The panels do not have to agree with one another — report what each panel actually shows, one answer per panel, even if the answer repeats or changes from panel to panel. Answer with exactly 8 answers separated by commas, in panel order, and nothing else.

Reply with exactly 8 comma-separated answers and nothing else.
